title: SSE trailer/whitespace causing dropped chunks - scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a recurring, low-frequency streaming failure where an SSE client (internal SDK + some 3rd party clients) sees missing final chunks. Hypothesis: trailing whitespace / unexpected bytes in the final chunk combined with proxy (Envoy) chunk-splitting causes client-side parser to drop the last event.

Observed symptoms:
- Customer reports final message in stream intermittently never arrives (client logs show connection closed, no final event).
- Server logs show 'stream closed normally' and a final flush; no obvious error on server side.
- Proxy (Envoy) metrics show occasional 1-2B chunk splits around connection close for the path.
- Repro is flaky locally but increases when we add gzip on the path or when using nginx as reverse proxy.

Why I think whitespace/trailer matters:
- Some SSE parsers are strict about event framing: they look for a '\n\n' (blank line) to mark end of event. If the blank line has spaces/tabs (e.g., "  \n"), some naive implementations treat it as non-blank and keep buffering until EOF. If EOF arrives after an intervening proxy split that leaves only whitespace in the last chunk, client may treat it as an unfinished event and discard on close, or raise 'unexpected EOF' then ignore buffered bytes.
- Observed server-side flush sequence sometimes sends: chunkA(ends with "data: foo\n"), chunkB("  \n") as a separate tiny chunk, then FIN. If the client trims whitespace it works; if not, it gets stuck.

Repro attempts / commands tried:
1) Raw netcat server that sends manual chunked frames to mimic behavior (works for deterministic repro):
   # start a simple TCP server (Linux):
   while true; do nc -l 127.0.0.1 8082 -q 1 <(echo -e "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n6\r\ndata: x\n\r\n2\r\n  \\n0\r\n\r\n"); done

   - Explanation: send a small chunk with data then send a chunk that is two bytes of spaces + newline as its own chunk, then 0 chunk. This reproduces a client that waits.

2) curl to observe raw bytes: (note --no-buffer to force streaming)
   curl -v --no-buffer http://127.0.0.1:8082/stream -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 2>&1 | sed -n '1,200p'

   - Look at chunked frames in verbose output. When proxied via nginx/Envoy this verbosity helps see split boundaries.

3) Node fetch quick client that shows buffering behavior and prints received "events" and raw bytes (run locally):
   const http = require('http');
   const req = http.request({host:'127.0.0.1', port:8082, path:'/stream'}, res => {
     res.setEncoding('utf8');
     res.on('data', chunk => {
       process.stdout.write(`CHUNK(${Buffer.byteLength(chunk)}) >${JSON.stringify(chunk)}\n`);
     });
     res.on('end', ()=> console.log('END'));
   });
   req.end();

   - Useful to see whether chunk sizes and content arrive as expected.

4) Go client with bufio.Reader to show how scanner treats trailing whitespace:
   resp, _ := http.Get("http://127.0.0.1:8082/stream")
   scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
   for scanner.Scan() {
     fmt.Printf("LINE(%d): %q\n", len(scanner.Text()), scanner.Text())
   }

   - If last blank line contains spaces, Scanner will produce a non-empty Text; parser expecting empty line will mis-handle.

5) Simulate Envoy chunk splitting with python raw socket: create an HTTP server that writes first chunk, sleeps, writes whitespace-only chunk then close. Reproduces behavior under artificial timing conditions.

Exact raw frames observed (from tcpdump capture of internal repro):
--- server -> proxy TCP payload (hex/display) ---
HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n5\r\ndata:\x20A\r\n\r\n2\r\n\x20\x20\r\n0\r\n\r\n
Client side sees: data: A\n (then a chunk with only two spaces and CRLF) then connection close. Some client parsers drop the event because the blank line is not truly blank.

Error snippets captured in client logs:
- "sse: incomplete event, connection closed"
- "parser: got EOF while scanning for blank line"
- In some SDK logs: "stream-parse-failed: trailing bytes ignored (len=2)"

Hypotheses / root causes to investigate:
- Downstream proxies (Envoy/nginx) are performing chunk boundary splitting that separates whitespace-only terminators into their own chunk. When combined with compressed responses or connection-level buffering, the client sees a whitespace-only chunk as the last non-data chunk and mishandles it.
- Our internal SSE parser (and some 3rd-party libraries) consider a line as 'blank' only if len(trimmed) == 0 OR if the raw line length == 0. Implementations that check raw length==0 will treat a line with spaces as not-blank and keep waiting.
- gzip/content-encoding may be interacting during flush such that the final newline is emitted in a separate chunk and gets trimmed incorrectly by the parser.
- Some clients ignore events if the event is not terminated by a completely blank line; so if a final blank line is whitespace-only they discard last event on close.

Potential mitigations / quick fixes:
- Server side: ensure we flush a proper '\n\n' (two raw bytes CRLF CRLF) as the final terminator. Explicitly write '\n' after the final blank line and flush. For chunked encoding, emit a 0-length chunk only after emitting a chunk containing an explicit '\n' without whitespace.
- Parser side: be more tolerant: consider a line blank if trim(line) == "" (i.e., ignore spaces/tabs). Add a final EOF handler that processes any buffered data as an event instead of silently dropping.
- Proxy config: disable chunk-splitting / buffering on the streaming route (Envoy: set http_stream_idle_timeout? adjust buffer limits). In nginx, set proxy_buffering off for SSE routes.
- Tests: add unit tests for the parser that feed it "  \n" as blank-line candidate and ensure final event is emitted on EOF.

Metrics to add to help diagnose in prod:
- Count of "tiny chunks" (<= 4 bytes) published per stream in final 200ms before FIN. Spike might correlate with failures.
- Histogram of chunk sizes for SSE endpoints (to detect split patterns).
- Parser-side warnings: increment counter when EOF occurs with non-empty buffer (i.e., potential dropped event).

Concrete next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add parser tolerant mode in SDK and run canary on a small percentage of traffic. (Evan to own small SDK patch)
- [ ] Add integration test that reproduces netcat chunk-frame described above (Lina to add in integration tests).
- [ ] Run controlled experiment: disable nginx buffering for one customer and check failure rate over 48h.
- [ ] Add logging in serving runtime: emit `stream.final_chunk_bytes` metric tagged with route/model so we can correlate.
- [ ] Check if gzip is enabled in the pipeline for affected customers and run the static replays.

Notes / random observations:
- This flaky failure seems more common on mobile SDKs and some older Node SSE parsers. Desktop browsers (EventSource API) are usually fine because native EventSource implementations already trim whitespace.
- One customer had an intermediate CDN that rewrites chunk boundaries; that surfaced the issue.
- I tried toggling keep-alive timeouts on proxy and saw a small reduction in occurrence but not elimination.

Scratch ideas for quick diagnostic endpoint:
- Create /debug/sse-repro that intentionally emits: data: A\n<chunk containing two spaces + CRLF> then close. Have it behind a flag so we can route customer traffic to it for repro.

If we get a clean repro we can do two fast patches: parser tolerance (safe) + server ensure-final-terminator (defensive). Parser change is lower-risk and should fix third-party client cases too.

Last tested: 2026-03-09 local with netcat + nginx in front (repro index ~1/3 runs).

Appendix: Minimal netcat server (one-liner) to reproduce locally:
   while true; do nc -l 127.0.0.1 8082 -q 1 <(printf 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n6\r\ndata: hi\n\r\n2\r\n  \r\n0\r\n\r\n'); done

(That one created a chunked response: chunk '6' contains 'data: hi\n', chunk '2' contains two spaces then CRLF.)

-- Aisha
